title: Addressing the alignment problem in transportation policy making: an LLM approach

bias_targets.methodology: Using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression models to analyze how community-level socioeconomic variables (such as income tiers, car ownership, and transit reliance) influence the transit policy preferences generated by LLM agents.

Incorporating the percentage of non-White residents as a demographic covariate in regression models to determine if minority status significantly impacts the policy voting behavior of simulated LLM agents.

Applying VADER sentiment analysis to the decision-making rationales generated by LLM agents to detect uniformly optimistic tones, which the authors hypothesize may reflect pretraining biases and an underrepresentation of marginalized community narratives.
